user.title: Add a Patternflow device
user.description:
The device answers to patternflow.local out of the box. If mDNS is unreliable on your network, use the IP address shown on the device's NETWORK screen (hold K2).

Running more than one panel? Each needs its own PF_OTA_HOSTNAME in net_config.h — there is no serial number to tell two boards apart, so the hostname is the identity.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Add this Patternflow device
zeroconf_confirm.description: Found a Patternflow panel at {host}. Add it to Home Assistant?

knob_control.title: Turn the knobs from Home Assistant?
knob_control.description:
Knob positions are always readable. Changing them is not: the panel's HTTP API has no knob endpoint, so a knob write has to go out over MQTT — and the panel only obeys knob and pattern topics while it is a Subscriber. It is currently "{role}" on {broker}.

Switching it costs something worth knowing: a Subscriber stops publishing its own knob turns, because the two roles are exclusive. You will still see the knobs move in Home Assistant, since that reading comes over HTTP and not from the topics.

You can change this later on the panel's own /mqtt page.

error.cannot_connect: Nothing answered as a Patternflow device at that address. Check that the panel is powered, on the same network, and that the address is right.

abort.already_configured: This device is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: Nothing answered as a Patternflow device at that address.
abort.duplicate_hostname: Another device is already set up under this hostname. Two panels cannot share one — give this one its own PF_OTA_HOSTNAME in net_config.h, reflash it, and try again. Adding it as it is would take over the existing device's entry.

init.title: Patternflow options
init.description: The panel's web server takes one connection at a time, and drawing pauses while it answers. Polling faster is not free — leave this alone unless you have a reason.

mqtt_compiled_out.message: This panel's firmware was built without MQTT, so its knobs cannot be set remotely at all.

no_broker.message: The panel has no MQTT broker configured, and its HTTP API has no knob endpoint. Point it at your broker on its own /mqtt page, then set its role to Subscriber.

not_subscriber.message: The panel only obeys knob topics while it is an MQTT Subscriber. Change its role on its own /mqtt page — note that a Subscriber stops publishing its own knob turns.

broker_unreachable.message: The panel is not connected to its MQTT broker, so a knob change would go nowhere.

mqtt_not_set_up.message: Home Assistant has no MQTT integration set up, which is what actually sends the knob change. Add it, pointed at the same broker as the panel.

mqtt_publish_failed.message: Publishing the knob change to MQTT failed.

knob_write_failed.message: The knob change could not be sent.
